newsitem.title: FRANCE: France confirms signed joint arms pact with Bonn.
newsitem.headline: France confirms signed joint arms pact with Bonn.

text.p: The French defence ministry confirmed on Thursday that it signed an agreement at a December 9 bilateral summit meeting with Germany on procurement orders for military helicopters and missiles.

The Le Monde newspaper reported earlier this week that the two governments would soon notify the Eurocopter joint venture of contracts for tooling up for production of the Tiger combat aircraft and would order an initial 160 units, equally shared between the two countries.
Eurocopter is 70 percent owned by Aerospatiale and 30 percent by Daimler-Benz Aerospace.

"The defence ministry confirms the fact that (French minister) Charles Millon and (German minister) Volker Ruhe signed on the margins of the Nuremburg meeting last December an agreement on bilateral arms programmes which set the framework for the coming weeks and months," a senior ministry spokesman told reporters.
He declined to give details of the agreement due to its "extremely sensitive" nature.
However, sources close to the ministry confirmed the details of the newspaper report.
Le Monde said France has set procurement for the Tiger at 215 units, while Germany wants 213. The Tiger comes in anti-tank and close-support versions.
France will also order 160 NH90 army tactical transport and naval helicopters, Germany 243.
France will also order a total 2,544 long-range Trigat anti-tank missiles for the Tiger, Germany will get 2,544.
An initial order for 1,800 Trigats for each country will be placed on a multi-year basis, at current prices.
Aerospatiale and Daimler-Benz are joint venture partners in the Trigat programme.
